sourceProject: FM27 Match Lab - runs FM27's own match engine headlessly and replays saved matches under controlled changes

method.design: Paired comparison: each condition changes one thing for the team and replays the same 10 saved matches on the same 30 seeds; the effect is the mean paired difference over 300 matches.
method.confidence: |t| >= 2 is about 95% confidence; |t| >= 3 is solid. A study with many conditions shows a few |t| of 2-3 by chance.
method.resolution: With 300 pairs, effects of about 0.1 points per game or 0.1 xGD can be detected. 'No clear effect' means below that resolution, never 'no effect'.
method.outcomes: Points per game is what matters but is noisier; expected-goal difference (xGD) is the most sensitive.

caveats: All bases are one Premier League club that finished lower-table, replayed against stronger teams: magnitudes describe that situation, not football in general.
Every condition shares one baseline, so all conditions of a study share that baseline's luck (up to about +/-0.05 expected points per condition).
Paired designs reduce noise only slightly: one change alters the match from the first touch.
These are match-engine results from simulation; they do not cover training, transfers, finances or morale beyond what is stated.

findings.claim: Pace is the most valuable attribute in the match engine
findings.per: +5 in-game points for the whole squad
findings.detail: Also +0.32 xG for, -0.19 xG against, +1.5 shots, more and better chances; possession share falls 0.9pp.

findings.claim: Acceleration is worth almost as much as Pace and improves both ends
findings.per: +5 in-game points for the whole squad
findings.detail: +0.24 xG for and -0.23 xG against, +1.7 shots, +1.3pp possession.

findings.claim: One point of Pace across the squad is worth about as much as 3-4 points of Dribbling; +5 Pace for the whole squad is roughly 13 points over a 38-match season
findings.per: +5 in-game points for the whole squad

findings.claim: Stamina is clearly worth having and helps both ends
findings.per: +5 in-game points for the whole squad

findings.claim: Dribbling is the best of the technical attributes and works through attack only
findings.per: +5 in-game points for the whole squad
findings.detail: +0.20 xG for, no effect on xG against.

findings.claim: Jumping Reach pays mainly in defence through aerial duels
findings.per: +5 in-game points for the whole squad
findings.detail: -0.21 xG against; conversion slightly negative.

findings.claim: Anticipation is the most valuable mental attribute measured, mostly defensive
findings.per: +5 in-game points for the whole squad

findings.claim: Work Rate is worth having but shows up as fewer goals against rather than more xG
findings.per: +5 in-game points for the whole squad

findings.claim: Finishing does not create chances, it converts them: xG is unchanged but goals above xG rise
findings.per: +5 in-game points for the whole squad
findings.detail: Points also rise (+0.11 ppg, t 2.3). Do not judge Finishing by xGD.

findings.claim: Concentration adds shots and is worth about +0.09 points per game at +5 for the squad
findings.per: +5 in-game points for the whole squad

findings.claim: Passing, Technique, First Touch, Crossing, Off The Ball, Tackling, Marking and Positioning show no clear match effect
findings.per: below this threshold, i.e. not resolvable
findings.detail: This is 'below the 0.015 xGD/point resolution', not 'harmful'. Do not rank players down for these; do not pay a premium for them either.

findings.claim: Most attributes are straight lines; the exceptions are Work Rate (has a floor), Jumping Reach (pays above roughly 9-12), and Pace/Acceleration which diminish above 12; Strength works through goals rather than xG
Tests run on a sample match with every attribute levelled to 12 exaggerate physical attributes and shrink mental ones; real matches reward Anticipation and Concentration
findings.detail: If a conclusion comes from a levelled-squad harness, distrust its mental-attribute ranking.

findings.claim: Decisions, Teamwork, Determination and Flair show no clear effect on results in any design tested
Current Ability does not affect the match: CA from 40 to 200 changes nothing measurable when attributes are held fixed, alone or together with Passing or Decisions
findings.detail: Any scouting or transfer score that ranks players by CA/PA is ranking by a number the engine does not read. Rank by the attributes that do move results (Pace, Acceleration, Stamina, Dribbling, Jumping Reach, Anticipation, Work Rate, Finishing).

findings.claim: Match sharpness is the single largest controllable factor: a squad at 50 percent sharpness loses about 1.03 points per game and one at 75 percent about 0.37, while the tested squads naturally sit at 90-100
findings.detail: Getting a rusty player back to full sharpness is worth roughly +0.10 to +0.16 points per game. Rotation and fitness management are worth more than any tactical tweak.

findings.claim: Match condition is the second largest controllable factor: a squad at 80 percent condition loses about 0.80 points per game and at 90 percent about 0.28, while natural values sit at 94-99
findings.detail: Full condition is worth about +0.13 to +0.18 points per game. Fatigue advice should outrank tactical advice.

findings.claim: Playing players out of position is expensive: capping every starting position rating at 10 costs about 0.85 points per game, and about 0.65 in the neutral rerun
findings.per: all starting position ratings capped at 10

findings.claim: Handing in-match decisions to the game's own AI instead of the assistant cost about 0.56 points per game and 0.91 xGD in the tested matches
findings.detail: Provisional: the setting was measured on one club's matches. Advise keeping normal assistant management rather than delegating to the AI.

findings.claim: The only team instruction with a confirmed effect is one to avoid: setting the pressing trap to show inside or outside instead of standard costs about 0.19 to 0.23 points per game and 0.30 to 0.40 xGD, confirmed on 1,200 pairs
Adding one step of attacking mentality costs about 0.12 points per game and 0.22 xGD, while moving more defensive showed nothing clear
findings.detail: Do not recommend a more attacking mentality for its own sake.

findings.claim: Weight, height, Current Ability, reputation, club cohesion and personality have exactly zero or no clear effect on match results (all |t| < 1.6)
findings.detail: This is the third independent confirmation that Current Ability is inert (see S20-CA-INERT). Never rank players for match impact on CA, PA, reputation, weight or height.

findings.claim: Team cohesion moves results a little: highest versus lowest cohesion is worth about +0.21 points and +0.32 xGD per game
Tactic choice is the largest tactical lever: best versus worst across all 17 tested tactics is about 0.86 points per game, and about 0.47 within the ten installed presets alone
Untrained tactical familiarity areas cost about 0.4 points per game
Attributes and tactical familiarity add up independently; good players do not need a familiar tactic to show it, and quality does not compensate for unfamiliarity
Chance creation and pressing intensity are the familiarity areas that matter most, about 0.08 expected points per game each when neglected (t 6-7); out-of-possession shape is third
findings.detail: Raising any area above 50 gains nothing measurable.

findings.claim: Gegenpress, Control Possession and Fluid Counter-Attack lead for a favourite, an underdog and a National League side (rank correlation 0.95); Park the Bus is last
findings.detail: Tactics matter most lower down the pyramid: about a 31-point swing across a season at National League level.

findings.claim: In a neutral-ground league every community tactic beat every FM27 preset; overall tactic strength predicted almost every head-to-head
findings.detail: Measured on synthetic reference squads, so this is a tactic-vs-tactic comparison with squad quality held constant.

findings.claim: Home advantage is real and worth about 0.36 points per game (1.54 home vs 1.18 away), about +0.21 xG
Home advantage depends on the ground: stadiums of 40,000+ give about +0.39 xG, smaller grounds about +0.15 to +0.18; pitch size does nothing
Morale showed no measurable effect on results
Pressure is the one hidden attribute with a clear effect; Consistency barely matters and is often not read by the engine
findings.detail: Dirtiness and Temperament drive cards.

findings.claim: Attribute value differs by position: Jumping Reach matters for centre-backs and strikers, Pace and Acceleration matter everywhere
findings.detail: From 50,000 random configurations (every attribute of every starter varied in every match). The playing style changes the sizes, not the order.

findings.claim: For goalkeepers, Agility and Reflexes are each worth about 0.8-1.1 goals a season per level
findings.per: one level of Agility or Reflexes

findings.claim: No single goalkeeper attribute is clearly decisive; raising all of them by +5 together is worth +4-5 points of save rate and +0.26 points per game, and a goalkeeper position rating of 10 concedes +0.69 goals per game
findings.detail: Playing a keeper badly out of position is far more costly than any single attribute.

findings.claim: Unfamiliarity in the in- or out-of-possession phase of a position costs nothing measurable; what costs is the player's other-position ratings and, for keepers, the goalkeeper rating
The attribute ranking holds at every squad strength (rank correlation 0.84) and does not reverse for favourites or underdogs
The same attributes lead from the Premier League down to the National League, with no attribute differing between divisions (p 0.86): Pace, Acceleration and Jumping Reach lead everywhere
Work Rate is a floor, not a gradient: below about 3 it costs results heavily and above 9 more is worth almost nothing
findings.per: below the knee at 3, versus 0.014 above it
findings.detail: Measured on the neutral-ground family (synthetic mid-table squads, familiarity 80, Gegenpress). Treat players under Work Rate 3 as a real problem and ignore the difference between 12 and 18.

findings.claim: Pace and Acceleration have no floor, only diminishing returns, with knees around 11 and 13: about 0.08 expected points per point below the knee versus 0.04-0.05 above
findings.detail: Taking an attribute from 1 to 20 is worth about 1.2 expected points per game in total, so the cheap points are below the knee.

findings.claim: Jumping Reach is flat until about 9 and then pays at roughly 2.5 times the rate; 12 to 18 is the single largest gain of any attribute over that span
findings.detail: Below 9 it is worth about 0.019 per point and above it about 0.047. This is why tall centre-backs and strikers are worth paying for.

findings.claim: Strength works through converting chances, not through expected goals: 1 to 20 is worth about +0.50 goals above xG per game and +0.69 points
findings.detail: Its xG contribution alone looks small (+0.18 expected points), so an xG-only model undervalues it.

findings.claim: Familiarity saturates early: by about half of the measurable per-area scale (a 0-100 byte per area) all areas already give +0.19 points and +0.28 xGD per game, and raising them further to 90 or 100 reproduced identical matches
findings.per: areas at about 50 versus the squad's own level
findings.detail: The game's 0-20 tactical familiarity bar is not what the match reads; the input is a per-area byte 0-100. Match exposure counts about half as much as training (engine weights 0.3 vs 0.6). Never advise pushing an area above about 50.

findings.claim: The whole familiarity floor-to-plateau range is worth about +0.5 points and +0.75 xGD per game, comparable to about +7 Pace across the squad, so it is real but second-order next to player quality
findings.detail: A just-switched tactic at about 20 of 100 costs roughly 0.20 points per game.

findings.claim: Training familiarity is worth about twice as much as match exposure per point, so advise training blocks over 'play matches to learn it'
findings.per: training point versus 0.0053 for match exposure

findings.claim: Tactic complexity is not a lever in the match: held constant it moves nothing measurable, so never advise simplifying a tactic to cover poor familiarity
Line of engagement, pressing trap and in-possession shape familiarity show no measurable effect; passing style and build-up are small
findings.detail: So do not recommend training those areas to improve results; the areas that pay are chance creation and pressing intensity, then out-of-possession shape.

findings.claim: Only one in-match tactical tweak had a clear effect and it is a cost, not a gain: Lock It Down is worth about -0.20 expected points and -0.24 xGD per game
findings.detail: Its intended late-game protect-a-lead use was not tested, so do not describe it as a way to close out a game.

findings.claim: Sending the goalkeeper up for set pieces concedes more in all three designs tested, about +0.19 to +0.28 goals against per game, because the keeper is caught upfield

No in-match tweak helps on average: the best average is zero, about eleven of them are within +/-0.03 expected points of nothing, and a tweak's cost depends on the base tactic so it cannot be transferred between tactics
findings.detail: Play With More Patience looked positive once (+0.19 xGD, t 2.5) then negative in two later designs: a multiple-comparison artefact. Do not present tweaks as upgrades.

findings.claim: Among installed presets start from Gegenpress, Control Possession or Fluid Counter-Attack for any club, but a well-built custom tactic beat all 23 tested tactics for its squad, so presets are a floor not a ceiling
findings.detail: Weight tactic advice by club level: the best-versus-worst preset gap is about 31 points a season in the National League, 26 at a top club and 17 for a bottom Premier League side. Judge tactics on expected points, because a side can beat its xPts by 4-13 points a season.

findings.claim: Pressure is the one hidden attribute with a clear effect, and it is a floor: Pressure 1 is worth about -0.15 expected points per game, while raising it to 20 gains almost nothing
findings.detail: About 6 points a season. Screen low-Pressure players out of high-stakes roles rather than chasing high Pressure.

findings.claim: Consistency is read only in some fixture and side combinations, so it must never be given a blanket weight in a player score
findings.detail: 240 of 320 league matches replay identically at Consistency 1, 10 and 20; where the engine does read it, a value of 20 was worth about +0.16 expected points. Treat it as a tie-breaker at most.

findings.claim: Dirtiness and Temperament move cards and nothing else: Dirtiness 20 is about +1.00 cards per game, and Temperament 1 adds about +0.52
findings.detail: No measurable effect on expected points. Use it for suspension risk, not for match-outcome weighting.

findings.claim: Passing has no measurable match value and can even hurt: adding +5 to a passing group reduced possession and completed passes under Tiki-Taka, while only direct styles benefited
findings.detail: Passing is about +0.011 xGD per point (t 1.4). A whole squad at Passing 1 does not do measurably worse. Do not pay a transfer premium for passing.

findings.claim: Attribute groups are carried by a single member, so spreading weight evenly across a group is wrong: Jumping Reach supplied +0.22 of the aerial group's +0.23 and Anticipation +0.11 of the defending group's +0.08
findings.detail: Together with S10-NO-COMBINATIONS this says: build an additive model, but weight the individual attributes by measurement rather than averaging within a group.

findings.claim: Concentration, Dribbling, Balance, Passing, Decisions, Strength and Finishing are straight lines across 1-20, so one constant per attribute is the right model shape
findings.detail: Only Work Rate, Pace, Acceleration, Jumping Reach and Stamina need a curve.

findings.claim: Pace and Acceleration come first in every position; one extra level on one player is worth about 0.12 to 0.21 expected points a season depending on position, and the physical group (Pace, Acceleration, Jumping Reach, Stamina) is the bulk of it
findings.per: +1 level on one player, best position (striker Pace)
findings.detail: Physical four summed per level per season: centre-back 0.73, striker 0.67, attacking midfielder 0.52, full-back 0.52, defensive midfielder 0.42. From 50,000 random configurations.

findings.claim: Jumping Reach is the most position-specific attribute and is strongly convex: about +0.32 expected points a season per level for a centre-back against +0.06 for a defensive midfielder, and almost nothing at level 7 versus about 0.29 at level 17
findings.detail: Do not model it as a linear per-point constant; it needs the curve (see S12-JUMPING-KNEE).

findings.claim: Do not pay for technical or mental attributes for match output: Passing, Technique, Tackling, Marking, Positioning, Crossing, Decisions, Composure, First Touch, Off The Ball and Flair are all within +/-0.04 expected points a season per level in every position
findings.per: upper bound, per level, every position
findings.detail: That is the resolution floor, so these are 'no measurable match value', not 'harmful'. They may still matter for the game's own ratings, squad rules and the user's preferences.

findings.claim: Conversion attributes are the exception expected points cannot see: Finishing is worth about +0.21 goals a season per level for a striker and Strength about +0.18 to +0.19 for strikers and wide attackers at unchanged xG
findings.detail: Any ranking built only on xG or xPts systematically undervalues finishers and strong players.

findings.claim: For goalkeepers only Agility and Reflexes are worth paying for: about -0.93 and -0.76 goals against a season per level, roughly 8.5 goals and 5 points a season for +5 on both
findings.detail: One on Ones, Jumping Reach, Tendency to Punch, Handling and First Touch showed no measurable effect for keepers.

findings.claim: A goalkeeper's position rating matters far more than his attributes: at rating 10 instead of his natural 20 he concedes about +0.69 goals a game and loses about 0.53 points a game, roughly 20 a season, nearly four times a full +5 on every goalkeeping attribute
findings.detail: Also: expected points are computed before the keeper acts, so xG/xPts rankings systematically undervalue goalkeepers. Rank keepers on goals against and points.

findings.claim: Home advantage is a step in stadium size, not a slope: below 40,000 capacity it is about +0.15 to +0.18 xG, above it about +0.39 xG; pitch length and width change nothing
findings.detail: Do not model it from attendance: there is no editable crowd field, the same stadium varies from -0.03 to +0.61 xG across opponents, and a single fixture is only known to about +/-0.24 xG.

findings.claim: A specialist whose neighbouring-position ratings are empty is worth less than his slot rating suggests: capping outfield starters' non-native position ratings costs about -0.30 expected points a game, against -0.10 for capping their native rating
Do not extrapolate these curves below attribute level 9: there Pace and Acceleration degrade about 50 percent worse than linear and Work Rate collapses
findings.detail: The measured curves are only trustworthy over the range the studies covered.

findings.claim: The studies use two incompatible designs: real saved fixtures with real squads, and neutral-ground tests with synthetic mid-table squads at familiarity 80 on Gegenpress. Numbers from the two are not directly comparable
findings.detail: A real-fixture effect and a neutral-ground effect measure different situations. When magnitudes across studies are combined into one model, check which family they came from first.
